title: Office Parameter Manifest
description: Five source-informed parameters an LLM front-end may safely modify for a proposed office scene, since current Infinigen does not provide a working standalone office room generator in this pipeline.
infinigen_entity: source-informed proposal; no working standalone Semantics.Office generator in current indoor constraint path

ceiling_height_m.description: Floor-to-ceiling clear height of the office.
ceiling_height_m.rationale: Ceiling height is included because it changes perceived openness and enclosure. Meyers-Levy and Zhu motivate ceiling height as a cognitive-processing variable, while Vartanian et al. connect ceiling height and perceived enclosure to beauty judgments and approach-avoidance decisions.

task_lighting.description: Normalized strength of task lighting in the office.
task_lighting.rationale: Task lighting is included because light exposure is relevant to visual comfort, alertness, mood, circadian regulation, and workplace functioning. The 0.0 to 1.0 range is a generator-facing lighting control rather than a direct empirical lux range.

openness.description: Normalized spatial openness of the office layout.
openness.rationale: Openness is included because perceived enclosure and spatial prospect are meaningful environmental-psychology constructs. This parameter gives the LLM a safe high-level spatial control without exposing wall segment IDs or solver constraints.

biophilia_count.description: Number of plant or nature-related entities placed in the office.
biophilia_count.rationale: Biophilia count is included because even a work-focused room can vary in the amount of restorative nature cueing it contains. This is a stronger and more defensible environmental-psychology parameter than a free hue slider, and the bounded count keeps the control interpretable.

visual_complexity.description: Normalized amount of visual detail, objects, and complexity in the office.
visual_complexity.rationale: Visual complexity is included because environments vary in how much information they contain, how organized they feel, and how demanding they are to process. The 0.0 to 1.0 range is a bounded generator control rather than a direct empirical complexity scale.
